messages:
Security Ops: @here Advisory: weve observed anomalous token usage patterns for a small set of vendor-facing service principals. Immediate actions required: rotate affected credentials, enable short-lived tokens, and run the audit checklist below. This is NOT a full compromise confirmation but were treating it as high-priority. :warning:

Threat Intel: Summary of findings: unusual geo-distributed calls from 3rd-party IP ranges to partner-facing endpoints between 03:00-04:30 UTC. Token Inventory flagged tokens with heavy usage and atypical TTLs. No data exfiltration evidence yet.

Platform SRE: Which principals are in scope?

Security Ops: We pushed a CSV to the policy page: https://internal.redwood/sec/token-anom-2026.csv. Primary scope: services that call external partner APIs and any roles with cross-account access. Token Inventory Bot will DM owners of flagged tokens.

Token Inventory Bot: automated-note: You own token_id tok-9f3b listed in token-anom-2026.csv. Please rotate or mark for exception within 48 hours.

CI Team: Some CI jobs fetch partner creds from Vault weekly. Is weekly rotation sufficient?

Threat Intel: For external-facing principals, effective TTL must be <=24h. Weekly rotates exceed our containment threshold. Short-lived credentials issued at job start are preferred.

Platform SRE: Quick rotation steps (example for Vault + AWS IAM):
```
# create new key
aws iam create-access-key --user-name partner-uploader
# update vault secret
vault kv put secret/partners/partner-a access_key=<NEW> secret_key=<NEW>
# rollout
kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/partner-uploader
```
Tag PRs with #sec-rotate and include smoke-test results.

Security Ops: Investigation playbook (short): 1) Run Inventory query for token usage (we posted SQL on the policy page), 2) Rotate flagged credentials, 3) Verify no abnormal logs post-rotation, 4) If unable to rotate, open an "anom-exception" ticket with compensating controls (IP allowlist, HSM, strict logging), 5) Preserve logs and enable enhanced audit retention for 30 days.

CI Team: We have one legacy runner that cannot assume OIDC yet. Opening exception ticket now with IP allowlist and a 30-day remediation plan.

Platform SRE: We'll assist with rotation and smoke tests. Schedule a 1-hr window if you want pairing.

Threat Intel: If you rotated, run a targeted traffic replay check against logs for the affected window. Use our quick grep helper: `rg "tok-9f3b|partner-uploader" /var/log/proxy/*` and check for external IPs we listed.

Security Ops: Timeline: immediate rotation recommended. Token Inventory Bot will perform a dry audit tonight and we will enforce revocation for any unrotated partner-facing tokens in 72 hours. Non-partner-facing long-lived tokens get a 14-day window.

deploy-bot: policy-change logged: token-usage-anomaly-response (id: pc-2026-21). See https://internal.redwood/policies/pc-2026-21 for playbook and CSV.

Security Ops: TL;DR action items: 1) Check CSV and token inventory, 2) Rotate partner-facing creds now to <24h TTL, 3) Migrate CI to ephemeral creds or OIDC, 4) File exception ticket if you cannot rotate, include controls and remediation dates.

Platform SRE: Acknowledged. Will start rotations and post progress.

CI Team: Starting rotations now, will update when smoke tests pass.

Security Ops: Thanks all. Well post an incident summary if more evidence appears. For urgent help ping @Platform SRE or @Security Ops directly.
